samples.summary: The nesting cap this PR now enforces on producers contradicts the canonical design doc's stated Goal and is recorded nowhere
samples.evidence: `docs-nested-tables.md:19` states as a Goal: "Recursive nesting with no hard depth limit (UI naturally limits via minimum cell width of 30 px)". This PR introduces `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH = 32` (packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts) and this delta extends it from a read-time guard into *producer* behaviour that is user-visible: `DocxImporter.convertTable` now DROPS `<w:tbl>` past the cap (docx-importer.ts:437, so imported content is silently lost, contradicting the doc's ".docx round-trip" goal), and `writeFullDocument` now THROWS for a document at the cap (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3261), a new failure mode of the `setDocument`/`setHeader`/`setFooter` contract that `docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:227,295` documents. No design doc under docs/design/ mentions the docs table-nesting cap at all: `docs/design/docs/docs.md`'s hardening section (lines 209-298) enumerates every other band/cap (row height, numeric attrs, slides group depth 32, `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH`) but not this one, and `docs-docx-import-export.md` says nothing about a depth limit. Per CONTRIBUTING the change belongs folded into the canonical subsystem docs (docs-nested-tables.md Goals + docs.md hardening + docs-collaboration.md store contract), not left undocumented. Note this is a NESTED design doc, so the broken-refs CI lane does not cover it either.
searchedFor: grep MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH across repo (no docs/design hit)

samples.summary: The backend v1 PUT writer — a duplicate producer of the same Yorkie tree — keeps its own, differently-bounded depth constant, so the producer cap this delta argues for is not enforced there
samples.evidence: The delta's stated design (`docx-importer.ts:244-256`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:3248-3258) is "cap the producer so the consumers are safe", and it caps the DOCX importer and the frontend full-document writer. But `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:150-200` is a verbatim second copy of `buildBlockNode`/`buildRowNode`/`buildCellNode` writing the SAME tree from a REST `PUT /content` body, and it received no cap; its only bound is `assertValidBlock`'s independent `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` (controller line 806) tested as `depth > MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` (line 443), i.e. it ADMITS 33 nested table blocks, one deeper than `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`'s `depth >= 32` truncation. Two writers now give two answers to "how deep may a table be", and the API answer produces exactly the document this delta declares must never exist: a table at a depth every reader materializes as rows-less, which `writeFullDocument` then refuses to rewrite, so it cannot be repaired from the editor. Cost is outside tidiness (silently truncated, unrepairable user content via an authenticated endpoint) and the divergence is introduced by this change.

samples.summary: Interactive producers (insert-table-in-cell, paste) still write past the cap through granular CRDT ops, so the producer-side argument only covers the DOCX path
samples.evidence: The delta justifies the import cap as "an imported document must never *contain* a table at a depth the readers truncate" (docx-importer.ts:432-441). The same invariant is not enforced on the editor's own producers: `Document.insertTableInCell` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:885, driven by editor.ts:4237) carries no depth check, and the paste sanitizer bounds only the *relative* depth of the pasted payload with its own separate constant `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` (clipboard.ts:71) — pasting an 8-deep table into an already-deep cell yields an absolute depth past 32. Those paths write via granular tree ops, bypassing `writeFullDocument`'s new refusal, so a user can still commit a table at a depth every reader shows as rows-less (silent content loss on next load) and which now also makes any later full write throw. Also a second, differently-scaled nesting constant in the same package for the same concept.

verdict.reason: Every claimed fact checks out. packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:150-200 is a second writer of the same docs Yorkie tree (its own header, lines 1-29, calls it "a deliberate, narrowly-scoped mirror of the writer/reader logic in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts") and its buildBlockNode/buildRowNode/buildCellNode take no depth and apply no nesting cap — line 166 maps every row unconditionally. The frontend twin does cap (yorkie-doc-store.ts:378-392, `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH ? [] : …`) and writeFullDocument even refuses such a document (3260-3271). The backend's only bound is the independent MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32 (docs-content.controller.ts:806) tested as `depth > MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` (line 443) with `depth + 1` recursion (line 491), so 33 nested tables are admitted — one deeper than the reader's `depth >= 32` truncation (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:219-229, table-nesting.ts:26). The path is reachable and unguarded: PUT /content (docs-content.controller.ts:163) runs assertValidDocsBody (line 190/304-325 → assertValidBlock at 315 and via assertValidHeaderFooter at 350) and then writeDocsRoot at line 213, which calls the uncapped builder. Result: two producers give two answers to "how deep may a table be", and the API answer persists a table whose rows no reader materializes and which the editor refuses to rewrite — silently truncated, unrepairable user content. That is the rubric's explicit `major` case (duplicated logic that diverges and gives two answers to the same question), and it is in the design-fit/duplication lane rather than a pure line-level logic bug, so no refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: The absence is real: no absolute nesting-depth guard exists on the editor's own producers. `Document.insertTableInCell` (document.ts:885-895) inserts via `store.insertBlockAfter` with no depth test, and its only caller (editor.ts:4227-4243) computes no depth. The paste path (text-editor.ts:4561-4576) calls `doc.insertBlockAfter` for a caret inside a cell, bounded only by the sanitizer's separate relative `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` (clipboard.ts:71, applied from depth 0 at clipboard.ts:308/404). The write-side cap in `buildBlockNode` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:378-392) is reached with the default `depth = 0` from both `insertBlockAfter` (:2335) and `insertBlock` (:2312), so it caps only the inserted subtree's own relative depth; the absolute-depth refusal (`hasTableAtNestingCap`, :446) has exactly three call sites, all inside `writeFullDocument` (:3260-3271). I found no guard in the memory store (memory.ts:102), Document.insertBlockAfter/insertBlockAt (document.ts:773,785), or any UI gating (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:225,914); the backend "nested too deeply" checks (docs-content.controller.ts:445) are on the REST body path, not the CRDT editor path. I weighed refuting as out-of-scope on the strength of docs-nested-tables.md:19-20 ("no hard depth limit... UI naturally limits") and table-nesting.ts:19-24, but those are a practical/narrative limiter predating the cap, not an enforcement point, so the producer-side invariant the delta asserts is genuinely applied only to the DOCX importer.
